analysis:
Examined the NemotronSuperServingPolicy.swift base and head text and the NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift patch. The only functional policy change is maximumEncodedBodyBytes, raised from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (head line 369). A new error mapping for .bodyTooLarge to MediaIngest.MediaError.mediaTooLarge is added in NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift (hunk @@ -175, lines 178-179).

Availability and resource exposure: the larger body bound feeds several memory-charge calculations. These are mediaChargeBytes (encodedCopies = 2x(40MiB/4*3) at head line 406), videoMediaChargeBytes (head lines 444-453) and encodedHeaderQuote. The per-request media reservation therefore grows, and defaultPrefixBankBytes already subtracts mediaChargeBytes(imageCount: 1) from the serving headroom. The charges are applied to the shared ledger and the existing exact-grant checks remain authoritative, so a larger charge fails closed (refusal) rather than overcommitting. The admissible body cannot exceed what transports deliver; the comment says 32 MiB for both localInferenceMaxUploadBytes and CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes. That claim could not be verified here because the transport code was not supplied. The 40 MiB bound is above those transport limits, so the transports remain the effective cap and the bound is not widened in practice. The relevant threat for resource exhaustion is TB-007/TB-002 DoS. No mapped threat definition is violated, and the ledger charge prevents unbounded admission.

Unverified contracts: I could not see NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding (where .bodyTooLarge is raised and where the encodedHeaderQuote and videoChargeBytes math lives), so I could not confirm there is no arithmetic overflow or under-quote at 40 MiB. I also could not confirm that the new MediaError.mediaTooLarge error leaks no content or is mapped to a proper client error. The message string is static and contains no user data. Plaintext-exposure concerns (T-050 inline video temp files) are not touched by this diff.

No security regression is identified from the supplied evidence. The remaining question for integration is whether the binding's quotes and the 25 MiB decoded media default are consistent with the 40 MiB body.
